thought.text: The controller reads `params[:username]`, but I sent `email`. Let me retry the login with the correct parameter.

reasoning_content: The user exists and is active. The issue is that the frontend is sending `params[:username]` — the controller uses `params[:username]`, not `params[:email]`. I sent `email` in the JSON body, but the controller reads `params[:username]`. Let me try using the `username` parameter. The login should work — the 401 is probably because I used the wrong parameter name. Let me retry with `username`.

action.command:
docker exec zammad-devcontainer-devcontainer-1 bash -c '
cd /tmp
CSRF=$(curl -s -c /tmp/cj2.txt http://127.0.0.1:3000/ | grep -oE "<meta name=\"csrf-token\" content=\"[^\"]+\"" | sed "s/.*content=\"//;s/\" *$//")
curl -s -b /tmp/cj2.txt -c /tmp/cj2.txt -o /tmp/login2.json -w "POST /api/v1/signin -> HTTP %{http_code}\n" \
  -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/v1/signin \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-raw "{\"username\":\"admin@example.com\",\"password\":\"test\",\"authenticity_token\":\"${CSRF}\"}"
echo "--- login2.json first 400 chars ---"; head -c 400 /tmp/login2.json; echo
curl -s -b /tmp/cj2.txt -o /tmp/sess2.json -w "GET /api/v1/signshow -> HTTP %{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/v1/signshow
grep -oE "\"email\":\"[^\"]+\"|\"login\":\"[^\"]+\"" /tmp/sess2.json | head -2
' 2>&1
